title: NY State Assembly · District 33
area: Southeast Queens, including most of Cambria Heights and Queens Village, and parts of St. Albans, Hollis, Bellerose, and Floral Park

context.text: Incumbent Clyde Vanel defeated Oster Bryan 71.1% to 28.4% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Bryan also holds the Working Families Party ballot line for the general election through a separate WFP primary victory.

candidates.name: Clyde Vanel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary 71.1% to 28.4% over Oster Bryan
candidates.currentRole: Member, New York State Assembly (since 2017); Chair, Banks Committee

summary.text: Clyde Vanel is the Democratic incumbent for Assembly District 33 in southeast Queens. An attorney, entrepreneur and pilot, he ran for the seat unsuccessfully in 2012 and won it in 2016. He chairs the Assembly Banks Committee and the Subcommittee on Internet and New Technology, focuses on emerging technology legislation, and is running for re-election after winning the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.

background.text: According to his official biography, Vanel was raised in Cambria Heights, Queens, with nine siblings.

He holds a Bachelor of Science in Aviation Administration and an Associate of Applied Science in Aerospace Technology from Farmingdale State College, where he was Student Government President. He earned a Juris Doctor from Boston University School of Law, where he was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Science & Technology Law.
He owns and operates Vanel Law Firm, P.C., where he practices intellectual property and business law, and operates TrademarkReady.com, a trademark-filing service.
He previously owned and operated a restaurant and lounge, Vanel on First, in Lower Manhattan for five years.
Vanel founded the New York Metro chapter of Black Pilots of America, Inc., which trains and exposes community members and youth to aviation, and is a member of the MIT AI Policy Forum.
He ran for Assembly District 33 in 2012, losing the Democratic primary to incumbent Barbara M. Clark and then losing to her in the general election on the More Jobs Party line.

He won the 2016 Democratic primary for the open seat and the general election, taking office in 2017; his official biography dates his service to his November 8, 2016 election. The district includes Cambria Heights, St. Albans, Hollis, Queens Village, Bellerose, and parts of Floral Park.

In the 2025-2026 session he chairs the Banks Committee and the Subcommittee on Internet and New Technology, and is a member of the Codes, Racing and Wagering, Rules, and Science & Technology committees, the Black Task Force, and the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus.

His official biography says he has sponsored legislation to create a robotics, automation and artificial intelligence commission, license high-risk AI systems, and create a cryptocurrency and blockchain study task force.
He has defeated Oster Bryan in Democratic primaries in 2018, 2020 and 2022, and again won the 2026 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Vanel says he has "stood up against the big banks to make sure families keep their homes from unscrupulous practices that lead to foreclosure" and advocates for "fair and affordable rents."
priorities.quote: stood up against the big banks to make sure families keep their homes from unscrupulous practices that lead to foreclosure

priorities.text: He lists consumer protection as a priority, describing his work "fighting against the scammers that steal millions of dollars from hard-working New Yorkers in person, over the phone and on the internet."
priorities.quote: fighting against the scammers that steal millions of dollars from hard-working New Yorkers in person, over the phone and on the internet

priorities.text: He champions expanding digital access, saying he works "to make sure that good quality affordable internet is a reality for all New Yorkers."
priorities.quote: make sure that good quality affordable internet is a reality for all New Yorkers

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Banks Committee and the Subcommittee on Internet and New Technology, and serves on the Codes, Racing and Wagering, Rules, and Science & Technology committees in the 2025-2026 session.

Sponsored A.3265, the "New York artificial intelligence bill of rights," which would give residents rights and protections regarding automated decision-making systems that affect their lives; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Science and Technology Committee.

Sponsored A.399, which would prohibit manufacturing, selling, or operating a robotic device or uncrewed aircraft equipped or mounted with a weapon in New York State; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Codes Committee.

Sponsored A.8101, the "New York Data Protection Act," which would require government entities and contractors to disclose personal information they collect about individuals; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Governmental Operations Committee.

Sponsored A.6268, the "New York public banking act," which would authorize municipal and local governments to form and control public banks for community economic development and infrastructure needs; as of January 2026 it remained referred to the Assembly Banks Committee, which Vanel chairs.
Won re-election in 2024 with 98.9% of the vote against no listed opponent (write-in votes made up the remainder).

candidates.name: Oster Bryan
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to Clyde Vanel; remains on the general-election ballot on the Working Families Party line

summary.text: Oster Bryan is a Southeast Queens educator and civic leader who describes himself as a community organizer with close to 20 years of community service. He has challenged Clyde Vanel in Democratic primaries since 2018, lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, and is on the November ballot on the Working Families Party line.

background.text: Bryan was born in New York, New York, and, per his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, was raised in Southeast Queens.

He earned a bachelor's degree from Baruch College in 2001 and a graduate degree from Fordham University in 2010. In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he described a BBA in Finance from Baruch and an MBA in Finance from Fordham University/Peking University.

He worked for the New York City Employees' Retirement System (NYCERS) for eight years as a member of DC37. His listed profession is professor; in 2022 he described himself as an independent business consultant and adjunct professor of business and finance at Long Island Business Institute in Flushing, Queens.

He has run for Assembly District 33 before: in 2018 (including the Democratic primary, which he lost to Clyde Vanel 79.8% to 20.2%, and also as a Reform Party candidate), and in the Democratic primaries of 2020 and 2022, which he also lost to Vanel.

He describes himself as president of the St. Albans Civic Improvement Association and an educator and union member. His survey also lists affiliations with the Cambria Heights Civic Association, the Caribbean American Rep. Theatre, the Cambria Heights Toastmasters and the Eastern Queens Alliance.

According to his 2026 survey, he helped organize a free youth physics program on renewable energy, runs a free math program, and organizes civic, environmental justice and beautification projects in the district.

priorities.text: Bryan lists his three key campaign messages as taxing the wealthy for economic justice, fully funding public schools and expanding free CUNY/SUNY access, and stopping gentrification and displacement.
priorities.quote: TAX THE RICH and deliver economic justice for the middle and working classes. FULLY FUND OUR PUBLIC SCHOOLS and pave the way for free CUNY and SUNY. STOP GENTRIFICATION and displacement of longtime residents by ending deed theft and making life in NYC affordable.

priorities.text: He says his campaign is about improving public services and making Albany policy more affordable for the district, describing his approach as being "present, listens, and gives the district a true voice."
priorities.quote: Our community deserves a representative that is present, listens, and gives the district a true voice in the decisions that are made in Albany.

priorities.text: He names education, housing, and climate/environment as the public-policy areas he is personally passionate about.

positions.summary: Lists taxing the wealthy for economic justice as one of his three key campaign messages.
positions.quote: TAX THE RICH and deliver economic justice for the middle and working classes.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website or other interviews were found.
